newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco taps Morgan Stanley for stadium bond.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco taps Morgan Stanley for stadium bond.

text.p: San Francisco Mayor Willie Brown said Tuesday that Morgan Stanley Group Inc will serve as underwriter for a proposed $100 million bond issue to finance a new football stadium.
In addition, Financial Security Assurance, a unit of Financial Security Assurance Holdings Ltd., will insure the proposed bond issue, Brown said at a press conference here.
Brown said the proposed bond issue would be structured to protect the city's general fund.
"The project will retire the indebtedness," Brown said.

San Francisco residents will vote June 3 on the $100 million lease revenue bond measure. The bond funds would help to finance the city's share of the proposed $525 million San Francisco 49ers football stadium and shopping complex.
Morgan Stanley said it had developed a finance plan under which the city would not be obligated to pay debt service on the stadium bonds if project revenues fell short of projections.
"We believe this is a very good credit and inherently doable," Morgan Stanely principal Robert Larkins said.
FSA said it reviewed the legal, credit and financial components of the proposed bond deal and is "confident that the proposed lease revenue bond financing can be structured with FSA insurance."
Mayor Brown, who supports the stadium issue, said he hoped the structure of the bond deal and the FSA insurance would convince "naysayers" to support the stadium bond measure on June 3.
